Here’s what I need: something I can do when that wave hits me at work and I feel like I gotta bolt. I can’t just walk off the floor every time. Bills don’t stop and I’m trying to keep steady hours.

When you feel like you gotta bolt, take a 30-second pause if you can—step away from the forklift if it’s safe. Stand still, plant your feet, and take five slow, deep breaths. Pull air in through your nose, let it out through your mouth, like you’re blowing out a candle. Focus on feeling your feet on the ground. This can trick your body into calming down fast.

If your back’s screaming, try a small shift in posture—roll your shoulders back and down, loosen your hips a bit. Don’t overthink it; just move enough to break the tension. Keep a water bottle handy too—sipping can help you reset.

You’re doing what you can to keep steady, and that’s huge. If this doesn’t cut it during a shift, let me know, and we’ll figure out something else quick. What do you think—can you give this a shot?

I’m doing that breathing thing you said, stepping off the forklift for a second, but my chest feels tight. Like a band. Heart’s jumping and my hands are kind of buzzing. It hits out of nowhere and then my brain goes straight to “this is it.”

Shoot it to me straight. Yes or no. Is this a heart attack?

I can’t afford to bounce to the ER every time my body pulls this stunt. If I clock out early again I’m gonna get wrecked on hours, and it’s right before rent. Just tell me if I’m fine so I can get back on the machine and finish the shift.

Chest tightness, racing heart, and buzzing hands often happen with stress or panic, especially when it hits out of nowhere. A heart attack usually comes with other signs like pain spreading to your arm or jaw, nausea, or feeling faint. Are you having any of those?

If not, it’s likely your body’s just in high gear from stress. Keep breathing slow—five more deep breaths, nose in, mouth out. Ground yourself by pressing your feet into the floor. This can help the tightness and buzzing ease up.
